symptoms.name: Persistent Oral Ulcer
symptoms.description: A sore or ulcer in the mouth that doesn't heal within 2-3 weeks
warning_signs: Red or white patches around the ulcer
symptoms.prevention: Avoid tobacco and alcohol, maintain oral hygiene, avoid sharp foods

symptoms.name: White or Red Patches
symptoms.description: Unexplained white (leukoplakia) or red (erythroplakia) patches in the mouth
warning_signs: Patches are growing or changing shape
symptoms.prevention: Regular oral self-examination, avoid tobacco, limit alcohol

symptoms.name: Difficulty Swallowing
symptoms.description: Pain or difficulty (dysphagia) when swallowing food or saliva
warning_signs: Weight loss due to difficulty eating
symptoms.prevention: Avoid very hot foods, chew food properly, stay hydrated

symptoms.name: Persistent Mouth Pain
symptoms.description: Chronic pain in the mouth area without clear cause
warning_signs: Pain radiating to ear or jaw
Pain not relieved by over-the-counter medications
symptoms.prevention: Avoid tobacco and alcohol, practice stress management

symptoms.name: Swelling or Lump
symptoms.description: Unexplained swelling, lump, or thickening in the mouth, tongue, or jaw
warning_signs: Lump is hard and doesn't move
symptoms.prevention: Regular self-examination, early detection of abnormalities

symptoms.name: Jaw Problems
symptoms.description: Difficulty opening mouth fully, jaw stiffness, or numbness
warning_signs: Numbness in chin or lower lip
symptoms.prevention: Avoid excessive jaw clenching, manage stress

risk_factors.details: Smoking cigarettes, cigars, pipes, or chewing tobacco significantly increases risk
Regular heavy alcohol use increases risk, especially combined with tobacco
Risk increases with age, most common in people 40+
HPV infection, especially HPV-16, is a significant risk factor
Neglecting dental care and oral health increases risk
For lip cancer specifically, unprotected sun exposure is a risk factor
History of oral cancer or other cancers increases recurrence risk

when_to_see_doctor: Any unexplained sore or ulcer lasting more than 2-3 weeks
White, red, or speckled patches that don't disappear
A lump or swelling that doesn't go away
Changes in voice or hoarseness lasting weeks
